image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of the head and upper neck of a Nile crocodile resting on dry, earthy ground. The image focuses heavily on the texture of the skin, showing detailed osteoderms (bony scutes) and scales. The snout is visible in profile, with teeth interlocking along the jawline. The eye is open and alert. The background consists of blurred soil and dry vegetation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The profile view clearly shows the tapered, V-shaped snout characteristic of crocodiles, distinct from the U-shaped snout of alligators.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The lower jaw teeth are clearly visible protruding upwards and fitting into notches/alongside the upper jaw, demonstrating the correct interlocking anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned high on the skull. While the pupil shape is hard to resolve at this resolution, the positioning and general morphology are correct. No obvious artifact in the eye structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostril openings are visible at the distal end of the snout, consistent with biological facts.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The neck and top of the head show prominent, raised bony scutes with a rough texture, matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of greys and browns, and the texture is visibly rough and cracked, consistent with reptile skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside (ventral surface) is not visible in this angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Nile Crocodile vs. other crocodilians) based on snout shape and scale pattern.
To analyze the micro-texture of the scales for signs of AI 'smearing' or repetitive pattern artifacts common in generated reptile skin.
To ensure the teeth are distinct entities and not fused with the jawbone or gums, a common failure mode in AI generation.

focus_areas: Integrity of individual teeth and gum line
Consistency of scale patterns (no sudden melting or repetition)
Boundary sharpness between subject and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the upper and lower jaw. AI often struggles with the specific 'interlocking' geometry of crocodile teeth. Also, verify if the texture on the neck scutes maintains logical continuity or if it dissolves into noise near the edges of the frame.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
